Before you start

Built for people
who like to tinker.

This is an experimental preview you run on your computer. Bring your own accounts and start with dialing disabled.

01 / Your computer

A local service.

Docker Compose, uv, Node and Codex CLI run the service and reasoning worker. The setup guide has a prompt for Codex to help.

02 / Your accounts

Voice + phone connection.

You need OpenAI API access, a Twilio number, HTTPS/WSS tunnels, and eligible ChatGPT custom plugin access. Check registration access before buying services.

03 / Your limits

Start small.

Set what Dots may share and agree to. Calls can be incomplete, and unfamiliar phone menus or unclear speech can cause mistakes.

Read the test coverage and known limits ↗

A few details

Before the
first call.

What does it cost?

Dots uses your OpenAI and Twilio accounts. OpenAI charges for API voice usage; Twilio charges for the phone number and calls. Your tunnel service may also charge. Codex reasoning uses your ChatGPT plan’s allowance, which is separate from API billing. Call budgets use estimates rather than live billing.

Does it need access to my email?

No. You can supply the facts in the brief. Connected read tools are optional, require your own authentication, and must be allowed for the call.

Where does my data go?

The service keeps encrypted call records locally. Model requests go to OpenAI and phone audio travels through Twilio. Connected tools and tunnels have their own data handling. Worker exchange files rely on local file permissions. Read the data and retention details.

Is the walkthrough a real call?

It is a scripted, silent illustration with fictional people, email and delivery details. No call or inbox lookup happens on this page. Its timing is compressed.

How do I get help?

Start with troubleshooting or report a reproducible issue. Share your version and a redacted error. Keep credentials, phone numbers, transcripts and private account details out of public issues.
